name: Open Face Chinese Poker (OFCP)
description: Open Face Chinese Poker is a partition game where players receive 13 cards over several rounds and place them face-up into three hands: Back (5), Middle (5), and Front (3). Hands must be in descending strength (Back â‰¥ Middle â‰¥ Front) or the player fouls. Players score by winning hand comparisons and earning royalties for premium hands. Fantasyland rewards QQ+ in Front with 13 cards dealt at once next hand.

history.origins: OFCP originated in Russia and Finland in the early 21st century. It was introduced to the poker circuit by Russian players in Paris in early 2012.
timeline: 2012: Introduced at Aviation Club, Paris; spreads to US and Europe.
2013: First major OFC tournament at PokerStars Caribbean Adventure.
Present: Staple of high-stakes side games and mobile apps.
history.cultural: Known as 'Gambler's Chess' due to visible information and complex hand rankings.
history.evolution: Pineapple (3 cards per turn, set 2, discard 1) became the dominant competitive format. Fantasyland was added as a popular house rule.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Each player has a board with 13 slots (Back 5, Middle 5, Front 3).
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 5 cards face-down. Players set them face-up. Then each player draws 1 card at a time (8 rounds), placing each in Back, Middle, or Front. Cards cannot be moved once placed.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, chips or score sheet, agreed stake per point.

rules.objective: Score more points than opponents by winning hand comparisons and earning royalties. Avoid fouling (Back < Middle or Middle < Front).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Initial deal**: 5 cards each, set face-up into the three hands. 2. **Draw phase**: Clockwise, each player draws 1 card, exposes it, and places it in one hand. 3. **Repeat** until all 13 cards are set. 4. **Showdown**: Compare Back vs Back, Middle vs Middle, Front vs Front against each opponent. 5. **Foul**: If Back < Middle or Middle < Front, you score 0 and pay 6 pts per opponent. 6. **Scoring**: 1 pt per hand won; 3 pt scoop bonus; royalties for straights, flushes, full houses, etc. 7. **Fantasyland**: QQ+ in Front (without fouling) gives 13 cards dealt at once on the next hand.

strategy.basic: Don't foul. Build a strong bottom hand early. Front hand: pairs or trips only.
strategy.intermediate: Push for Fantasyland: QQ in Front is worth the foul risk. Track opponent cards to know dead outs.
strategy.advanced: Outs calculation: if 8 spades are visible and you need one for a flush, switch to safe setting. Monte Carlo for hand-strength simulation.
tips: Pairs belong in Middle unless Bottom is already set or better.
In Fantasyland, prioritise staying in (Trips Front, Quads Back).
